- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 38.18, 36.84) — model fails to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price retraction.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30), while true prices often dip or stabilize.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent low prices — fails to adjust downward when history shows recent dips.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true price volatility — underestimates short-term volatility spikes.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early peaks and underestimate late troughs.
- Model exhibits “lagged” behavior — forecasts lag behind true price movements by 2–5 days in downward trends.
- Overconfidence in recent history — model overweights recent high prices, underweights recent lows.
